title: Create a 301 redirect without losing a page's traffic or causing a 404
objective: Redirect or remove a URL cleanly — every source URL accounted for, every destination verified, no orphan links or new 404s.
steps: Identify every place the source URL is referenced: sitemap entries, internal links, menu/footer links, and any known backlinks.
Add a row to the redirect-map tracker (data/redirect-map.json) — source, target, reason, owner, approval status — before touching anything live. No redirect goes live without a tracker row.
Confirm the target URL is correct, live, and actually the best-matching replacement for the source's intent.
Get explicit approval on the source-to-target row before publishing anything.
Implement one redirect at a time — never batch multiple redirects in a single pass.
Verify the resulting status code is 301 (not 302), and that there is no redirect chain (source should resolve in a single hop to the final live destination).
Update the XML sitemap and re-crawl the affected area to confirm no new 404s or orphan links were introduced.
Mark the tracker row resolved with the verification date and evidence (crawl export or screenshot).
sourceNote: Derived from docs/wordpress-safety.md (one change at a time; verify status codes and no 404s) and the redirect-shaped tasks already in data/tasks.json (Pleasant Grove removal, 109-page tiering).

title: Verify structured data (JSON-LD) the way AI and search crawlers actually see it
objective: Confirm schema is present, accurate, and machine-readable in raw HTML — not just in the rendered page.
steps: Open View Source for the page (Ctrl+U or equivalent) — never rely on the browser inspector/rendered DOM alone.
Locate the JSON-LD <script> block(s) directly in the raw HTML response, confirming they are not injected only after JavaScript executes.
Confirm the schema type(s) present match what the page needs (Organization, LocalBusiness, Service, Breadcrumb, Article, or Person as applicable).
Confirm every NAP field in the schema exactly matches the live Google Business Profile listing — no discrepancies in name, address, or phone.
Validate the markup with the current official rich-results/schema validator tool (not a cached or third-party mirror).
Report pass/fail per page type, and flag any assumption based on a deprecated or unsupported rich-result feature.
sourceNote: Derived directly from docs/ai-search-rules.md (schema must render in raw HTML; verify against current official docs).

title: Change a NAP or Google Business Profile field without creating conflicting citations
objective: Update a listing field (name, address, phone, hours, category) so every source of truth stays consistent — GBP, site schema, and citations.
steps: Read-only: capture the current live NAP, category, and hours across GBP, the website, and any known top citations before proposing a change.
Draft the proposed change with a clear reason (closure, phone change, hours update, new service category, etc.).
Never use a CallRail dynamic tracking number as the public GBP/citation phone number.
Present the before/after for approval — do not apply the change speculatively.
Mikey applies the approved change directly in Birdeye/GBP — an agent drafts, it does not log in or publish.
After the change is live, confirm it is consistent across GBP, site schema, and the website's visible NAP.
sourceNote: Derived from docs/wordpress-safety.md (never use CallRail number as public NAP) and the LOCAL-phase tasks already in data/tasks.json (GBP cleanup, exteriors listing update).

title: Build a new location, service, or exteriors page that matches brand and GEO formatting from day one
objective: Ship a new page that is on-brand, genuinely differentiated, and answer-ready — not a templated clone.
steps: Confirm the URL, nav placement, and market mapping as an approved structure before building anything.
Pull the existing Avada brand tokens/template so the new page matches the site exactly — Avada/Fusion Builder is the page builder, not Elementor.
Write genuinely differentiated copy for this page — no cloned paragraphs shared with similar pages.
Add a 40-60 word direct-answer intro at the top of the page.
Add accurate LocalBusiness/Service/Breadcrumb schema and verify it per the schema-verification procedure.
Build the page in Draft and show a Preview link for approval.
Leave real image placeholders for Mikey's own photos rather than presenting stock/generic images as real project photos.
Publish only on explicit approval.
sourceNote: Derived from the CONTENT/EXTERIORS-phase task patterns already in data/tasks.json (Boise page, Exteriors hub, individual service pages) and docs/wordpress-safety.md.

title: Hand a task to a Claude Code or Cowork session manually
objective: Move a task to Doing and hand it off yourself — the dashboard no longer auto-launches anything, so know the manual copy/paste flow and how findings come back.
steps: Before handing off, confirm the task's title, note, and execution steps are accurate — that exact content becomes the brief.
Move the card to Doing (drag on the board, or POST /api/tasks with col: "doing") — this only saves the task's state, it does not launch or open anything.
Open the task's "Cowork execution plan" and click "Copy Cowork brief" to copy the full operator brief to the clipboard.
Open a Claude Code or Cowork session yourself and paste the brief as the opening message.
Let the session work through to one of: Done, Draft ready, Blocked, or Needs approval, per the Final Report Format baked into the brief.
Bring findings back through you: paste observations into the Memory tab (POST /api/memory/append), add unverified claims to data/verification-queue.json, and log decisions in memory/decisions.md.
Only move the card to Done once the deliverable and verification are actually confirmed — not just because the session reported success.
sourceNote: Derived from docs/cowork-contract.md and memory/decisions.md (the 2026-07-16 decision removing the auto-launch feature that dec-secure-launch had hardened).

title: Orient a new agent session (Claude Code, Codex, or Cowork) before it touches this repo
objective: Make sure any session working in this repo reads the right context before acting on a Bartlett fact or touching the live site.
steps: Read docs/README.md for the system overview — what each data/memory/docs file is for.
Read data/site-facts.json and memory/decisions.md before using any Bartlett fact (served markets, NAP, claims, review counts, rankings, page status).
Treat data/tasks.json and data/cadence.json as the execution source of truth for what to work on.
Read the safety docs relevant to the work at hand: docs/wordpress-safety.md, docs/ads-safety.md, docs/ai-search-rules.md.
Check data/verification-queue.json for open, unresolved claims before treating anything as settled.
sourceNote: Derived from the READ FIRST section already baked into every Cowork brief (public/brief.mjs buildPrompt) and docs/README.md.

title: Edit a data/*.json file directly without corrupting the brain
objective: Make a direct edit to a data file (outside the dashboard UI) safely, when the UI doesn't cover the change needed.
steps: Prefer the dashboard/API paths (POST /api/tasks, /api/cadence, /api/archive) when the change is something the UI already supports — they validate automatically.
For a direct file edit, make the change, then immediately run `npm run validate`.
If validation fails, fix the file and re-run — never leave or commit a data file that fails validation.
Remember direct edits do not get the server's automatic pre-write backup — the safety net for a direct edit is validation plus normal git history.
sourceNote: Derived from docs/README.md (writeValidated / backupThenWrite path) and scripts/validate.mjs.
